notes_for_us: A required literal string in the world has nowhere to live. The user asked for exact text — "inspired by McDonald" — and the handoff can only describe it in a sentence to an image model, which is the one consumer that reliably garbles text. This is the second prompt in the batch whose most specific instruction is the one least likely to survive.

The boats are the racers and the only geometry the prompt describes, and Racing has no option for the racing vehicle itself — startpoint-line and spawn-grid describe where they sit, not what they are. Same hole as the ball in the car-soccer prompt earlier in this batch.
Real-world brand content arrived with no flag. Whether we build a McDonald's-branded map is a policy question, and the handoff has no field that would let a later step notice it was asked for.

notes_for_us: Racing's options table has no pickup row of any kind, and the pickup is the defining feature of the platform's most-copied racing style. Both coins and item boxes had to come from options.md, where they are worded for Obby and Shooter. A genre whose shortlist misses the thing every prompt in its most popular subgenre asks for is a shortlist problem, not a catalogue one — the Circuit Racing preset would be the natural place to fix it.

The three maps are structurally identical circuits differing only in dressing, and the segment record can only say that through per-segment theme. There is no way to say 'same track kind, three skins', so a reader cannot tell this from three genuinely different layouts.
'Make a map in a mushroom first' is a typo for forest. I read it rather than asking, which was right, but it is worth knowing the intake path silently repairs prompts.
